summary: With an execution environment, install collections in a playbook-adjacent ./collections directory (ansible-galaxy collection install ... -p ./collections) or build them into the EE with ansible-builder; for other directories set ANSIBLE_COLLECTIONS_PATHS plus a volume mount. Playbooks hang on vars_prompt or pause because navigator runs them like automation controller; disabling playbook-artifact creation allows interaction.
questions: Where should collections go when using ansible-navigator with an execution environment?
Why does my playbook hang on vars_prompt in ansible-navigator?
How do I use pause prompts with ansible-navigator?

answer_card.title: Collections and prompts in ansible-navigator
answer_card.answer_md:
**Collections with an EE:** install them next to the playbook, for example `ansible-galaxy collection install ansible.utils -p ./collections`, or build them into the EE with Ansible Builder. For another directory, set `ANSIBLE_COLLECTIONS_PATHS` and add a volume mount.

**Playbook hangs on `vars_prompt` or `pause`:** navigator runs playbooks the way automation controller does. Disable playbook artifact creation (`--pae false`) to run in an `ansible-playbook`-compatible way that allows user input.
